c.tagline: Korea's coastal city of beaches and seafood.

emergency.note: Dial 1330 for the 24-hour Korea Travel Helpline with English interpreters who can bridge to emergency services.

hood_landmark.Haeundae: Haeundae Beach's broad crescent of sand
hood_landmark.Seomyeon: the Seomyeon underground shopping arcade and food alleys
hood_landmark.Gwangalli: Gwangalli Beach's night view of the lit Gwangan Bridge

avoid.reason: Texas Street opposite Busan Station gets seedy late at night, and summer beach crowds at Haeundae attract pickpockets.

hood_desc: Haeundae is Busans upscale seaside resort district with a famous beach, luxury high-rise hotels and lively nightlife, ideal for first-time visitors and beach lovers who want a polished vacation base.
Seomyeon is the central transit, shopping and nightlife hub packed with restaurants, bars and department stores, best for travelers who want maximum convenience and nonstop energy.
Gwangalli offers a relaxed beach lined with trendy cafes and bars framed by the glowing Diamond Bridge, suiting younger travelers who like seaside nightlife with a local feel.
Nampo-dong is the historic downtown of street food, Jagalchi fish market and BIFF Square cinema culture, perfect for foodies and shoppers who want old Busan character.
Gwangbok is the bustling retail and street-food quarter around Gwangbok-ro near Gamcheon Culture Village, great for budget travelers and shoppers who enjoy a busy pedestrian scene.

water.note: Tap water meets national safety standards, though locals commonly prefer filtered or bottled water.

transit.pay: Get a T-money or Cashbee card (Korea's nationwide transit cards) for about ₩4,000 (~$3) at convenience stores (GS25, CU, 7-Eleven) or subway machines, then load cash and tap in/out. Base subway fare is about ₩1,500 (~$1.10), rising with distance, with free transfers to buses.
transit.hours: The subway runs roughly 5:30am to midnight, with exact times varying slightly by line.

transit.m: Busan-Gimhae Light Rail + Metro Line 2 to Seomyeon or Nampo, about 50 min
Airport city bus (route 307) toward downtown, about 60 min

landmarks: Haeundae Beach
Korea's most famous urban beach, backed by a skyline of skyscrapers, iconic for sunrise shots and summer crowds.
Gwangalli Beach
A scenic beach famed for its night view of the illuminated Gwangan Bridge stretching across the bay.
Gwangan Bridge
A dramatic suspension bridge that lights up in changing colors at night, a signature Busan skyline shot.
Jagalchi Market
Korea's largest seafood market, alive with fishmongers and fresh catch, offering vivid slice-of-life photography.
Gamcheon Culture Village
A hillside village of colorful stacked houses and murals, often called Busan's 'Machu Picchu' for its photogenic terraces.
Haedong Yonggungsa Temple
A rare seaside Buddhist temple perched on coastal rocks, combining vivid temple architecture with crashing waves.
Taejongdae
A cliffside natural park on Yeongdo Island with dramatic sea cliffs and a lighthouse, popular for coastal photography.
Busan Tower (Yongdusan Park)
A 120m tower atop a hilltop park in the city center, offering classic elevated views over the port and downtown.
Oryukdo Skywalk
A glass-floored viewing platform on a cliff overlooking the iconic Oryukdo islets, a thrilling vantage point over the sea.
Beomeosa Temple
A major mountainside Buddhist temple of the Jogye Order, prized for its traditional architecture amid forested slopes.

train.note: There are no international trains from South Korea - the sealed border with North Korea blocks all overland rail. Domestically, KORAIL's KTX high-speed trains run from Busan Station to Seoul in about 2 hr 30 min; book in English on the KORAIL Global site. SRT high-speed services also link Busan with Suseo in southern Seoul. Busan Station is central, right by the port, so ferry connections are an easy walk or short taxi ride.

bus.note: No international buses are possible from South Korea because of the closed North Korean border. Domestic express coaches leave from Busan's Nopo (Central) and Sasang (Seobu) terminals - the main operator is KOBUS/Express Bus (https://www.kobus.co.kr/main.do). Nopo is on Busan Metro Line 1, so getting there without a taxi is straightforward.

ferry.note: All international sailings leave from the Busan Port International Passenger Terminal near Busan Station; the Shimonoseki and Osaka services are overnight crossings and the Fukuoka boat runs both overnight and daytime, so carry your passport and allow time for immigration. Fast day boats to Tsushima (Japan) are run by Korean operators such as Miraejet and Daea. JR Kyushu's Queen Beetle fast ferry to Fukuoka was permanently withdrawn in December 2024, so the Camellia Line ship is now the main Busan-Fukuoka link.

half.name: Geoje Island

half.name: Daegu
half.blurb: Lively inland city known for herbal markets, modern murals and nearby mountain temples.

half.name: Ulsan
half.blurb: Coastal city with bamboo groves, seaside cliffs and traditional whaling-village heritage.
